name: Yombe
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: De Clercq, L. 1907, Grammaire du kiyombe (Goemaere, Brussels); also Mabiala, J.-N. 1999 comparative Kikongo phonology thesis

new_statements.quote: Cette intensité mélodique ne doit pas être confondue avec ce qu'on appelle en général l'accent d'intensité ou même, tout simplement, l'accent. 20. En Kongo, les mots ont, dans la règle, l'accent principal (étymologique) sur la syllabe radicale et un accent secondaire (rythmique) assez fort sur la pénultième. L'intensité mélodique peut affaiblir plus ou moins l'accent étymologique sur la syllabe radicale, mais celle-ci ne peut jamais devenir atone.
new_statements.translation: This melodic intensity must not be confused with what is generally called the intensity accent or, simply, the accent. 20. In Kongo, words as a rule have the main (etymological) accent on the root syllable and a fairly strong secondary (rhythmic) accent on the penult. Melodic intensity may more or less weaken the etymological accent on the root syllable, but the latter can never become unaccented.
new_statements.citation: Laman, K. E. 1936. Dictionnaire kikongo-français avec une étude phonétique décrivant les dialectes les plus importants de la langue dite kikongo. Mémoires de l'Institut Royal Colonial Belge, Section des sciences morales et politiques, t. II. Bruxelles: Institut Royal Colonial Belge.
new_statements.locator: Étude phonétique, §20, p. XIV (archive.org item dictionnairekikongofrancais, scan leaf 12; leaf n = page n+2, verified at leaves 38 = XL and 58 = LX); scanned lines 1041-1050
new_statements.rule_in_words: Main (etymological) accent on the root syllable of the word, i.e. the first syllable of the stem after the class prefix; a fairly strong secondary rhythmic accent on the penult. Tone ('melodic intensity') can weaken but not remove the root accent.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary (rhythmic) accent on the penultimate syllable ('un accent secondaire (rythmique) assez fort sur la pénultième'); Laman & Heinitz 1922 §2 p. 1: 'The rhythmic accent is a secondary accent that always falls on the penult.'
new_statements.exceptions: Laman 1936 §20: melodic intensity can weaken the root accent but the root syllable 'ne peut jamais devenir atone'. Laman & Heinitz 1922 §2: if the ultima gets strong stress the penultimate rhythmic accent is weakened; §28: the strong stress may be placed on different syllables because pitch and sentence position influence it; monosyllabic nouns can transfer strong stress to the prefix (bula ~ bwala).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('les mots'). The rule is stated for 'Kongo' as a whole, i.e. Laman's Kikongo cluster whose reference dialect C is the central Bas-Congo variety around Mukimbungu; Kiyombe (de Clercq's variety) is covered as the western dialect domain (O, §13, pp. LXXXVI-LXXXVIII) without a separate accent statement. Laman's 'accent' is dynamic stress interacting with lexical/grammatical tone; the language is tonal (his 'tons musicaux', §§9-18) and long vowels are contrastive (§8). The only Yombe-specific source opened, de Clercq 1907 p. 451, marks a 'tonic accent' with an acute but gives no placement rule.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted rule is Laman's statement for 'Kongo' (the Kikongo cluster; his reference dialect C is the central Bas-Congo variety around Mukimbungu, i.e. Koongo/Manyanga Kikongo, probably koon1244), not a Yombe-specific statement. Laman explicitly treats Kiyombe (the variety de Clercq described at the Kangu mission, Mayombe, Belgian Congo) as his western dialect domain O (§13, pp. LXXXVI-LXXXVIII), and the companion work Laman & Heinitz 1922 lists Mayombe among the dialects covered, so the rule is asserted to hold for Yombe but was not demonstrated on Yombe data. De Clercq 1907 (on file), the only Yombe-specific description opened, marks a 'tonic accent' with an acute (p. 451) but gives no placement rule. WALS's 'Iwoyo' (kwy, Mingas 1994) is mapped to yomb1244 but has no stress datapoints.

sources.note: Étude phonétique §20, p. XIV (scan leaf 12): in Kongo the main (etymological) accent falls on the root syllable and a fairly strong secondary (rhythmic) accent on the penult; melodic intensity (tone) can weaken but never remove the root accent. §8 p. XI: a syllable with rising or falling tone is also long. Kiyombe of de Clercq is treated as the western dialect domain (O), §13, pp. LXXXVI-LXXXVIII, with segmental and morphological notes only, no separate accent remark.

sources.citation: Laman, K. E. (with W. Heinitz). 1922. The musical accent or intonation in the Kongo language. Stockholm: Svenska Missionsförbundet.
sources.note: §2 'Dynamic accent', p. 1 (scan leaf 26): 'The root-accent always falls on the root-syllable... The rhythmic accent is a secondary accent that always falls on the penult. If the final syllable (ultima) gets strong stress, the rhythmic accent is weakened'; prefixes as a rule do not affect the accent. §28 p. 34: 'The strong stress in the Kongo language may be placed on different syllables... because pitch and position in the sentence may have a strong influence upon the accent.' Preface p. IX lists Mayombe among the dialects covered, but the description is of Kongo generally.

sources.citation: de Clercq, Aug. 1907. Grammaire du Kiyombe. Anthropos 2: 449-466, 761-794.
sources.note: Ch. I 'Notions préliminaires', p. 451 (scan leaf 557): vowels are long or short; 'Les voyelles non marquées seront considérées comme brèves, celles qui sont longues seront indiquées par le trait-au-dessus p. e. ā; l'accent tonique par ´ p. e. á.' Only a marking convention, no rule for where the tonic accent falls; speakers 'aiment à traîner un peu sur les voyelles longues en haussant légèrement la voix d'une façon presque chantante'. p. 767: past definite of ba 'be': 'accent tombe sur bá: ndibá, ubá'. Variety: Mayombe around the Kangu mission, Belgian Congo.
